attractions.name: Hopewell Mound Group trails
attractions.description: Trails cross the earthwork landscape and enter woodland containing a surviving part of an original earthen wall. Gravel and mulch surfaces include some climbs despite much of the site being fairly level.

length.method: NPS introduction: "the trail is about 2.5 miles long with a few changes in elevation". Approximate site trail distance; not claimed as a measured perimeter-only loop.

attractions.accessibility: Only a short sidewalk from the parking area is paved. Other trails use mulch, pebbled dirt, or grass and include elevation changes and a narrow wooden bridge.

attractions.name: Mound City Group nature trail
attractions.description: A nature trail circles the reconstructed mound group, passes through young woodland, and follows the Scioto River side of the site. Interpretive signs within the mound enclosure explain the earthworks.
attractions.accessibility: Forest paths have mulch and grass surfaces. Concrete steps connect to the lower paved river walk; the upper river walk is flat and gravel covered.

attractions.name: Hopeton Earthworks overlook trail
attractions.description: A self-guided trail climbs to an overlook of the earthwork landscape. Interpretive mowing outlines the former circle and square, helping visitors understand features whose surviving earthen walls are low.
attractions.accessibility: Only the short entrance section is paved. The remaining grass, mulch, and gravel trails have uneven terrain with ascents and descents.

history.event: Mound City Group National Monument was proclaimed, establishing the predecessor of Hopewell Culture National Historical Park.
The visitor center was dedicated, with archaeologist John L. Cotter delivering the keynote speech.
Mound City Group National Monument was renamed and redesignated Hopewell Culture National Historical Park.

attractions.name: Acadia Gateway Center
attractions.description: The Acadia Gateway Center is a new intermodal transit and welcome center that serves visitors to Downeast Maine and Acadia National Park. It is located on Route 3 in Trenton three miles north of Mount Desert Island. Visitor facilities include an Island Explorer bus stop, day-use parking, and an 11,000-square-foot welcome center with park and tourism information, Park Store, waiting area, and restrooms. The AGC will promote ridership on the Island Explorer from there and throughout the bus system and assist visitors in planning their trip to Downeast Maine. The National Park Service will staff the welcome center to provide visitors with a sense of arrival and orientation to the park, encourage use of the Island Explorer to visit the park, and ensure visitors have a park entrance pass and Cadillac Summit Road vehicle reservation. The AGC is owned by the State of Maine and operated by the Maine Department of Transportation in partnership with the National Park Service, Downeast Transportation Inc., and Maine Office of Tourism.

attractions.description: A paved circuit approaches the base of Lower Yosemite Fall and offers views of the falls and Yosemite Creek. Spray is strongest during high spring and early summer flows.

length.method: NPS Trail Overview: "Distance: 1 mile (1.6 km) loop". Entire loop; no conversion or doubling.

attractions.accessibility: The eastern portion of the paved loop is wheelchair accessible when free of ice and snow; this statement does not apply to the entire loop.

attractions.name: Cook's Meadow Loop
attractions.description: Paths and boardwalks cross the Yosemite Valley meadow landscape, with views of Yosemite Falls, Half Dome, Glacier Point, and Sentinel Rock. The circuit includes road crossings.

length.method: NPS Trail Overview: "Distance: 1 mile (1.6 km) loop". Entire loop; no conversion or doubling.

attractions.accessibility: NPS describes the trail as wheelchair accessible when not covered in snow. Boardwalks can be slippery when wet or frosted.

attractions.name: Mirror Lake Trail (lake and back)
attractions.description: The shorter Mirror Lake outing follows a paved service road to the lake below Tenaya Canyon. Water is usually fullest in spring and early summer; the separate longer circuit continues beyond the paved section.

length.method: NPS Trail Overview: "Distance: 2 miles (3.2 km) round trip to lake and back". The lake-and-back option only, excluding the separately listed five-mile loop.

history.event: President Abraham Lincoln signed the Yosemite Grant, setting aside Yosemite Valley and the Mariposa Grove for public use and recreation under California's administration.
An Act of Congress established Yosemite National Park.
Yosemite Valley and the Mariposa Grove were transferred from California to the federal government and included in Yosemite National Park.

attractions.name: Zion Canyon Visitor Center
attractions.description: Linked by the official park history & culture page. See the source for its relationship to the park, details and current access.

attractions.name: Zion Nature Center
attractions.description: Details and accessibility information for the Zion Nature Center, which opens seasonally during the summer.

attractions.name: Watchman Trail
attractions.description: From the Zion Canyon Visitor Center, the trail follows the river before climbing sandy, rocky terrain to a viewpoint over lower Zion Canyon and Springdale. There are drop-offs along the route.

length.method: NPS Duration text: "Watchman trail is 3.3 miles (5.3 km) roundtrip." Published whole-hike distance; not derived from the separately assessed overlook and loop segments.

attractions.accessibility: The unpaved route is sandy, rocky, and uneven, with drop-offs. NPS assesses the approach and overlook loop as separate segments with steps and steep grades.

attractions.name: Riverside Walk
attractions.description: A paved path follows the Virgin River from the Temple of Sinawava into narrowing sandstone walls. It reaches the beginning of The Narrows; entering the river is a separate continuation.
attractions.accessibility: Paving is irregular in places, minor drop-offs occur, and sand can make the concrete slippery. NPS reports steep sections; paving alone does not establish wheelchair suitability for the whole route.

conflicts.detail: The accessibility survey gives 1 mile one way; the spring 2026 guide gives 2.2 miles round trip.

attractions.name: Pa'rus Trail
attractions.description: The main trail connects Zion Canyon Visitor Center with Canyon Junction along the Virgin River, offering Watchman views and interpretive exhibits. It is shared with bicycles and leashed pets.
attractions.accessibility: NPS describes the main route as wheelchair accessible. The optional unpaved connector to the Human History Museum is not designed for wheelchairs.

conflicts.detail: The individual page describes 3.5 miles end-to-end and 1.6 miles one way in its survey; the spring 2026 guide labels 3.5 miles round trip.

history.event: A presidential proclamation established Mukuntuweap National Monument, protecting the area that became Zion National Park.
The monument was enlarged and renamed Zion National Monument.
An Act of Congress established Zion National Park.

attractions.description: Linked by the official park history & culture page. See the source for its relationship to the park, details and current access.

attractions.name: History Grove
attractions.description: History Grove is one of the only old growth ponderosa pine forests in New Mexico.

attractions.name: Beaver Pond Nature Trail
attractions.description: Yucca flats and a ridge above Lime Kiln Creek lead down a steep hillside to beaver ponds and evidence of dam-building.

attractions.name: Bighorn Head Gate
attractions.description: A gravel path reaches remnants of an early-twentieth-century irrigation system. Water levels can submerge the head gate.

attractions.name: Three Mile Access
attractions.description: A riverside path follows the Bighorn River to a cottonwood grove, with opportunities to observe fishing and waterbirds.

attractions.name: Visitor Center Pond
attractions.description: A concrete loop behind the Lovell visitor center circles a former solar-reflection pond now returning toward marsh habitat.
attractions.accessibility: The official guide labels this route accessible; detailed slope, surface and assistance requirements are not provided.

attractions.name: Sykes Mountain Trail
attractions.description: A rugged desert-mountain ascent reaches overlooks of Bighorn Canyon and Horseshoe Bend; summer heat is a particular concern.

attractions.name: Mouth of the Canyon Trail
attractions.description: Views of the Pryor and Bighorn Mountains contrast with red Chugwater outcrops near Horseshoe Bend.

attractions.name: State Line Trail
attractions.description: Juniper scrubland and limestone plateaus lead to a canyon-rim view, with a connection toward Ranger Delight.

attractions.name: Ranger Delight
attractions.description: A faint road cut and saddle lead toward the canyon rim from near the Montana state line.

attractions.name: Sullivan's Knob Trail
attractions.description: A canyon-rim walk passes near the ancient Bad Pass Trail, seasonally used by Indigenous travelers between the Bighorn Basin and Northern Plains.

attractions.name: Two Eagles Interpretive Trail
attractions.description: Interpretation explains stone circles left by Indigenous families who weighted tipi edges with stones. These cultural resources must remain in place.
attractions.accessibility: The official guide labels this route accessible; detailed slope, surface and assistance requirements are not provided.

attractions.name: Lower Layout Creek Trail
attractions.description: An old two-track road follows the area south of Layout Creek, with views into Layout Creek Canyon.

attractions.name: Upper Layout Creek Trail
attractions.description: A steep hike explores Layout Creek’s water and ranching landscape, whose irrigation history includes Erastus Ewing’s 1897 water claim.

attractions.name: Barry's Island Trail
attractions.description: A former two-track road circles Chain Canyon, once used by cattle rustlers, toward Barry’s Island; high reservoir water may cover parts of the route.
